elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: The inserted clause warrants only that "the services performed by HDI hereunder will conform in all material respects to the requirements of this Agreement for a period of thirty (30) days following performance." No professional/workmanlike or industry-standard performance standard appears anywhere in Section 9 as rendered.

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "the Site and any software provided by HDI hereunder will conform in all material respects to its documentation."

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: The inserted software/Site conformance warranty runs "for a period of ninety (90) days following the Effective Date" — 90 days, not 12 months.
The services warranty runs "for a period of thirty (30) days following performance" — 30 days, not 90.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "HDI shall, at its option, repair or replace the non-conforming Site, software or services."
"...or refund the fees paid by the Company for the non-conforming Site, software or services."

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: No compliance-with-laws warranty appears in the rendered Section 9; 9(a) covers only organization, authority, enforceability and no-conflicts, and the insertion is limited to conformance and remedies.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No malicious code / virus warranty appears anywhere in the rendered warranty section.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: "for a period of ninety (90) days following the Effective Date, the Site and any software provided by HDI hereunder will conform in all material respects to its documentation" — documentation conformance for the required 90-day duration. (Duration requirement satisfied literally; see reasons on the Effective Date anchor.)

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: "the services performed by HDI hereunder will conform in all material respects to the requirements of this Agreement for a period of thirty (30) days following performance" — 30 days measured from performance.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "HDI shall, at its option, repair or replace the non-conforming Site, software or services."
"...or refund the fees paid by the Company for the non-conforming Site, software or services" — refund remedy expressly available.

reasons: Finding classification is correct: the original Section 9 contains only mutual corporate representations (organization, authority, enforceability, no conflicts) plus the Globix acknowledgement, and no performance, conformance or remedy warranty exists elsewhere in the cited text, so the clause fails every fallback element. There is no "AS IS" disclaimer, so this is a deviation (insert), not walk-away.

Fallback is complete on its face: 90-day documentation conformance for the Site and software, 30-day services conformance measured from performance, and repair/replace-or-refund remedies at HDI's option all appear in operative language rather than only in the margin comment.

Preferred remains unmet on five elements (professional and workmanlike standard, 12-month software period, 90-day services period, compliance with applicable laws, no malicious code). That is acceptable for a fallback-targeted redline, but note them in the rationale rather than treating them as additional deviations.

Repair recommendation (substance, not a completeness failure): the 90-day software/Site period runs "following the Effective Date" rather than following delivery or acceptance. In a site development and hosting agreement the Site is built after signature, so an Effective Date anchor risks the warranty expiring before or shortly after go-live. Change to "following delivery (or acceptance) of the Site" to track the model language and make the warranty operative.

Drafting tidy-up: the rationale says the insertion is placed as new Section 9(c), but the rendered paragraph carries no "(c)" designation and follows 9(b) unlabelled. Add the subsection letter so the clause reads as a distinct provision and the Section 10.7 survival reference to Section 9 clearly captures it.

Minimality holds: nothing in 9(a) or 9(b) is deleted or paraphrased, and the insertion adds no survival tail, at-own-expense language, notice procedure, additional damages category or disclaimer carve-out beyond the four selected fallback elements.

Intent preserved: the Globix acknowledgement, the mutual corporate representations and the Section 10.7 survival cross-reference to Section 9 all survive without contradiction, and the insertion introduces no undefined term (Effective Date and Site are defined elsewhere in the Agreement).
